_README: Physical materials, and materials DERIVED from vanilla ones.
materials[]  patches a VANILLA asset in place -- changes that surface
everywhere in the game. Only to feel a number out. Anything
shipped from here that is no longer declared gets pruned, or
the override outlives the decision to make it.
derived[]    builds NEW assets beside the vanilla ones. Two shapes:
material.existing  -- a material authored in the editor;
we only wire its PhysMaterial.
material.template  -- clone a vanilla INSTANCE and reparent.
WHY AN INSTANCE. A Material carries compiled shaders and no pak pipeline can
compile one. An INSTANCE is pure data: it inherits its parent's shaders and
overrides only what it names, and PhysMaterial is overridable.
AN INSTANCE WITH NO PhysMaterial INHERITS ITS PARENT'S. Mat_Snow and
Mat_Road_Snow are parented to MI_curbWhite, so without this wiring they would
drive like a kerb -- silently, since nothing reports it.
PARENT MATTERS AS MUCH AS PhysMaterial. An instance with no overrides looks
exactly like its parent, so these are parented to the vanilla snow material --
authored against MI_curbWhite they rendered as grey kerb.
A Vector2D is written (X;Y) with a SEMICOLON: --set splits pairs on commas.
fx_map_entries patches DataAsset/FX.uasset, which maps a surface to the wheel
effect the game spawns on it. Vanilla maps Dirt, Grass, Sand and Mud and has
NO ENTRY FOR SNOW -- that, and nothing else, is why snow threw no particles.
EMotorTownSurface::Snow exists (7) and our physical materials already report
it; the table just never used it.
This is a VANILLA override, so snow sprays everywhere in the game, not only on
Arini. The effect is the dirt one for now because the game ships no white
spray of its own.

derived._: Packed snow where people drive: 25% shallower than the agreed (12.5,50). 15 path meshes.
Untouched wilderness snow: 10% deeper than the agreed (12.5,50). 23 landscape/path meshes. Speed and resistance stay as tuned -- only DEPTH is scaled, since depth is what reads as sinking.

Dirt is snow divided by three: (9.375;37.5) -> (3.12;12.5). Vanilla ships PM_DirtRoad with NO digging block at all and PM_Dirt at depth 0.5-3, which is why the dirt reads as solid and bumpy. Resistance matches snow so depth is the only variable between the two surfaces. PARENT LEFT ALONE: unlike the snow instances, these are authored -- two scalar parameters, a vector parameter and base property overrides on M_BaseColor. Reparenting them to a vanilla dirt material would discard that look. Only the PhysMaterial is wired here.

Dirt is snow divided by three: (13.75;55) -> (4.58;18.3). Vanilla ships PM_DirtRoad with NO digging block at all and PM_Dirt at depth 0.5-3, which is why the dirt reads as solid and bumpy. Resistance matches snow so depth is the only variable between the two surfaces. PARENT LEFT ALONE: unlike the snow instances, these are authored -- two scalar parameters, a vector parameter and base property overrides on M_BaseColor. Reparenting them to a vanilla dirt material would discard that look. Only the PhysMaterial is wired here.

particle_variants._: Snow spray cloned from P_TireSmoke, not the dirt effect. Tire smoke is already a white smoke sheet -- the right SHAPE for kicked-up powder -- where the dirt effect is clods that stay reading as dirt however you tint them. Colour and spawn rate are still data, so both are tunable here.
